tasks.title: Memoise wapor_plan_time_slices() and wapor_temporal_codes()
tasks.notes: Distinct from 7.3 (which covers .load_metadata_catalog()). wapor_plan_time_slices() and wapor_temporal_codes() are both pure/deterministic given identical args but are not memoise::memoise()-wrapped, unlike the 3 structurally identical examples already in the package (wapor_generate_urls in api_client.R:367, wapor_variable_metadata in metadata.R:466, .load_metadata_catalog_cached in wapor_metadata_cache.R:192). Benchmarked 2026-09-17: not a CPU bottleneck by itself (~0.1-0.2s even for a 9-year daily-only D plan, 324 rows via `Rscript.exe` R-4.4.1 local run) but repeated identical calls -- e.g. wapor_run_monitoring() looping variables for the same season window, or repeated re-runs of seasonal AETI/ETc extraction scripts during iteration on the citrus (177 farms, Mar-Feb) and Savola (75 fields, 4 seasons) projects -- redo the same greedy interval decomposition every time. Fix: rename current body to wapor_plan_time_slices_internal()/wapor_temporal_codes_internal(), wrap with memoise::memoise() following the existing api_client.R pattern exactly, keep the exported name and signature unchanged. memoise is already an Imports dependency, no new packages needed. Add a cache-hit regression test (call twice with identical args, assert identical() result) and confirm the full test-plan_wapor_time_slices.R suite (20 tests) still passes. User asked to log this for later review/implementation in a future session, not implemented yet.

tasks.title: Fix dashboard crash on board_claim.ps1 BOM output
tasks.notes: load_board() read agents-board.json as plain utf-8; board_claim.ps1's Set-Content -Encoding utf8 always writes a BOM on Windows PowerShell, so every board update made the dashboard crash with JSONDecodeError on next load -- verified by relaunching it and hitting the exact traceback. Fixed by reading with utf-8-sig. Re-verified: relaunched, HTTP 200, no traceback in log, direct load_board()-equivalent script confirms correct task/status data. Stopped the verification instance afterward.

issues.title: Dashboard crashes on every board_claim.ps1 update (UTF-8 BOM)
issues.summary: app.py's load_board() decoded agents-board.json as plain utf-8. board_claim.ps1 (PowerShell Set-Content -Encoding utf8) always writes a UTF-8 BOM, which json.loads rejects outright -- meaning the dashboard had been broken since the first board_claim.ps1 call ever made against the file, surfaced only now because coord-board-v1's original smoke test ran before any board_claim.ps1 write existed. Fixed by decoding with utf-8-sig (tolerates BOM or no BOM). Verified by relaunching and confirming HTTP 200 with no traceback, plus a direct check that task data renders correctly.
